title: He Escaped Through a 6-Inch Food Slot
style: Dillinger/McNair flat cartoon-silhouette poster style, cuts locked to the music beat (ESCAPED theme re-used); CC/PD place photos; Choi shown only as a silhouette (no licensed photo)
lines: A grown man escaped from a police cell through a hole six inches tall. The slot they used to pass him his food.
September 17th, 2012. Daegu, South Korea. Five in the morning, inside Dongbu Police Station.
In one cell sat Choi Gap-bok, a career criminal held on a robbery charge. He had spent more than twenty years of his life behind bars.
And all that time, he kept his body flexible. The press would later call him the yoga master.
His cell had a food slot. Eighteen inches wide. Just six inches tall.
Days before, the cameras caught him practicing. Three times, he pushed his head and chest through the slot.
Then he got a tube of ointment from another detainee. He rubbed it on his head, his body, and the bars.
That morning, three officers were on duty. Two were asleep. The third was on the internet.
Choi slid head first into the slot. Shoulders. Chest. Hips. In less than a minute, he was out.
One investigator said he moved like an octopus. Then, police say, he squeezed through window bars barely five inches apart, and vanished.
He left a note behind. I'm sorry, it said. But I have to clear my name.
What followed was a massive manhunt. Thousands of police. Search dogs. Helicopters with thermal cameras.
He was spotted near Cheongdo. Then he disappeared again.
The newspapers gave him a new name. The Korean Houdini.
But many people didn't buy the story. Could an adult's head and shoulders really fit through six inches?
Some suspected something simpler. That the cell was left unlocked, and the police were covering it up.
September 22nd. Five days on the run. Police found him on the rooftop of an apartment building in Miryang.
This time, they locked him in a different cell. Its food slot was barely four inches tall.
He got six years in prison. But the question never went away. Yoga master, or police cover-up?
What do you believe? Tell me in the comments. Then watch ESCAPED number two, the cop who let a killer walk away. And follow for more escapes.

notes: Sources: Korea Times 'Korean Houdini jail-breaks again' (21 Sep 2012) and 'Police suspect still on the run' (18 Sep 2012); Korea JoongAng Daily 'Tightest of squeezes for a prison break in Daegu', 'Police hold back on details about Daegu's Houdini', 'Prison cell Houdini still on run despite manhunt'; Money Today 뉴스속오늘 (2026); Hankyung, Maeil, Kyunghyang, JKN 2012 coverage. Facts: escaped ~5:03 a.m. 17 Sep 2012 through a food slot 45 cm wide x 15 cm high; ointment on head/body/bars (police first said shampoo); CCTV showed three rehearsals pushing head and chest through; under a minute ('like an octopus', investigator); then 13.5 cm window bars (police account); two of three officers asleep, one on the internet; held on robbery-causing-injury charge (July 2012), moved to Dongbu on 12 Sep; ~23 years of past detention; 'yoga master' nickname; note: sorry / must clear my name; manhunt with thousands of police, dogs, thermal helicopters; seen in Cheongdo; caught 22 Sep 4:50 p.m. on an apartment rooftop in Miryang; re-jailed in cell 2 with an 11 cm slot; 7 years at first instance, 6 years on appeal (2013). Doubts: police withheld CCTV at first; suspicion the cell was left unlocked. No licensed photo of Choi: silhouette only.
